<description>
### Motivation & Background

Currently, the libbitcoinkernel C API does not provide a way to configure block pruning on  tck_ChainstateManagerOptions. Even though the underlying
ode::BlockManager::Options and
ode::ChainstateLoadOptions structures support pruning, libbitcoinkernel callers cannot pass a prune target.

Consequently, trying to open an existing pruned node's data directory fails during
ode::LoadChainstate() with:
``
[error] Failed to load chain state from your data directory: You need to rebuild the database using -reindex to go back to unpruned mode.
``
because chainman.m_blockman.m_have_pruned is true while options.prune defaults to false.

### Description of Changes

1. **C API (src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h)**:
   - Added  tck_chainstate_manager_options_set_prune_target(opts, prune_target_bytes).
   - Exposed  tck_PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL (matching
ode::BlockManager::PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL) for manual pruning (-prune=1).
   - Exposed  tck_MIN_PRUNE_TARGET_BYTES (550 MiB, matching MIN_DISK_SPACE_FOR_BLOCK_FILES).

2. **Kernel Implementation (src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp)**:
   - Implemented  tck_chainstate_manager_options_set_prune_target().
   - Validates that prune_target_bytes is either 0 (unpruned),  tck_PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL, or >= btck_MIN_PRUNE_TARGET_BYTES.
   - Sets m_blockman_options.prune_target = prune_target_bytes and m_chainstate_load_options.prune = (prune_target_bytes > 0) under LOCK(opts.m_mutex).

3. **C++ Wrapper & Tests**:
   - Added SetPruneTarget() in src/kernel/bitcoinkernel_wrapper.h.
   - Added boundary tests in src/test/kernel/test_kernel.cpp (verifying rejection of < 550_MiB, acceptance of minimum, manual, and unpruned values).

Fixes #35627.
</description>

<commits>
223e2a3185 kernel: Add function for setting prune target in ChainstateManagerOptions

Currently, libbitcoinkernel's C API does not expose any mechanism to
configure the block pruning target on btck_ChainstateManagerOptions,
even though the underlying node::BlockManager::Options and
node::ChainstateLoadOptions fully support pruning. Consequently,
attempting to use libbitcoinkernel with an existing pruned datadir
fails during LoadChainstate() with an error directing the user to
reindex.

Introduce btck_chainstate_manager_options_set_prune_target() to allow
configuring the prune target on btck_ChainstateManagerOptions.

- Disabling pruning is represented by 0 (the default).
- Manual pruning is represented by btck_PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL (matching
  node::BlockManager::PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL).
- Automatic pruning requires at least btck_MIN_PRUNE_TARGET_BYTES (550 MiB,
  matching MIN_DISK_SPACE_FOR_BLOCK_FILES).

Setting a non-zero prune target sets opts.m_blockman_options.prune_target
and enables opts.m_chainstate_load_options.prune under the options mutex,
allowing libbitcoinkernel to open and operate on pruned datadirs.

Also adds C++ wrapper method SetPruneTarget() and unit tests validating
boundary behavior in test_kernel.cpp.

Closes #35627.

d42579ffb9 test: verify ChainMan construction with pruned and unpruned configurations
</commits>

diff --git a/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel_wrapper.h b/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel_wrapper.h

 class ChainView : public View<btck_Chain>
diff --git a/src/test/kernel/test_kernel.cpp b/src/test/kernel/test_kernel.cpp
index 6c98b8ea05..de626add6f 100644
--- a/src/test/kernel/test_kernel.cpp
+++ b/src/test/kernel/test_kernel.cpp
@@ -894,7 +894,17 @@ BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(btck_chainman_tests)
     BOOST_CHECK(chainman_opts.SetWipeDbs(/*wipe_block_tree=*/true, /*wipe_chainstate=*/true));
     BOOST_CHECK(chainman_opts.SetWipeDbs(/*wipe_block_tree=*/false, /*wipe_chainstate=*/true));
     BOOST_CHECK(chainman_opts.SetWipeDbs(/*wipe_block_tree=*/false, /*wipe_chainstate=*/false));
+    BOOST_CHECK(!chainman_opts.SetPruneTarget(btck_MIN_PRUNE_TARGET_BYTES - 1));
+    BOOST_CHECK(chainman_opts.SetPruneTarget(btck_PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL));
+    BOOST_CHECK(chainman_opts.SetPruneTarget(btck_MIN_PRUNE_TARGET_BYTES));
+    // Verify constructing chainman with prune target enabled
     ChainMan chainman{context, chainman_opts};
+
+    // Verify constructing chainman with unpruned target
+    TestDirectory unpruned_dir;
+    ChainstateManagerOptions unpruned_opts{context, PathToString(unpruned_dir.m_directory), PathToString(unpruned_dir.m_directory / "blocks")};
+    BOOST_CHECK(unpruned_opts.SetPruneTarget(0));
+    ChainMan unpruned_chainman{context, unpruned_opts};
 }
 
 std::unique_ptr<ChainMan> create_chainman(TestDirectory& test_directory,
diff --git a/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp b/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp
index f24a4e8da7..6c1fceaff8 100644
--- a/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp
+++ b/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp
@@ -1265,6 +1265,26 @@ void btck_chainstate_manager_options_update_chainstate_db_in_memory(
     opts.m_chainstate_load_options.coins_db_in_memory = chainstate_db_in_memory == 1;
 }
 
+int btck_chainstate_manager_options_set_prune_target(
+    btck_ChainstateManagerOptions* chainman_opts,
+    uint64_t prune_target_bytes)
+{
+    static_assert(btck_MIN_PRUNE_TARGET_BYTES == MIN_DISK_SPACE_FOR_BLOCK_FILES);
+    static_assert(btck_PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL == node::BlockManager::PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL);
+
+    if (prune_target_bytes != 0 &&
+        prune_target_bytes != btck_PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL &&
+        prune_target_bytes < btck_MIN_PRUNE_TARGET_BYTES) {
+        LogError("Failed to set prune target: target must be 0, btck_PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL, or at least %u bytes.", MIN_DISK_SPACE_FOR_BLOCK_FILES);
+        return -1;
+    }
+    auto& opts{btck_ChainstateManagerOptions::get(chainman_opts)};
+    LOCK(opts.m_mutex);
+    opts.m_blockman_options.prune_target = prune_target_bytes;
+    opts.m_chainstate_load_options.prune = (prune_target_bytes > 0);
+    return 0;
+}
+
 btck_ChainstateManager* btck_chainstate_manager_create(
     const btck_ChainstateManagerOptions* chainman_opts)
 {
diff --git a/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h b/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h
index ce051bda7b..01d1736d9d 100644
--- a/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h
+++ b/src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h
@@ -1281,6 +1281,36 @@ BITCOINKERNEL_API void btck_chainstate_manager_options_update_chainstate_db_in_m
     btck_ChainstateManagerOptions* chainstate_manager_options,
     int chainstate_db_in_memory) BITCOINKERNEL_ARG_NONNULL(1);
 
+/**
+ * @brief Special value for prune_target_bytes indicating manual pruning mode
+ * (equivalent to the -prune=1 command line option).
+ */
+static const uint64_t btck_PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFULL;
+
+/**
+ * @brief Minimum allowed prune target in bytes (550 MiB). Prune targets below
+ * this (other than 0 for unpruned, or @ref btck_PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL) are rejected.
+ */
+static const uint64_t btck_MIN_PRUNE_TARGET_BYTES = 550ULL * 1024ULL * 1024ULL;
+
+/**
+ * @brief Set block pruning target in bytes for the chainstate manager.
+ *
+ * Setting this option allows libbitcoinkernel to operate on pruned block storage
+ * or configure automatic block pruning.
+ *
+ * When set to 0, pruning is disabled. If enabled, the target must either be
+ * @ref btck_PRUNE_TARGET_MANUAL for manual pruning, or at least
+ * @ref btck_MIN_PRUNE_TARGET_BYTES (550 MiB).
+ *
+ * @param[in] chainstate_manager_options Non-null, created by @ref btck_chainstate_manager_options_create.
+ * @param[in] prune_target_bytes         Pruning target in bytes (0 to disable pruning).
+ * @return                               0 if the set was successful, non-zero if the target is invalid.
+ */
+BITCOINKERNEL_API int BITCOINKERNEL_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT btck_chainstate_manager_options_set_prune_target(
+    btck_ChainstateManagerOptions* chainstate_manager_options,
+    uint64_t prune_target_bytes) BITCOINKERNEL_ARG_NONNULL(1);
+
 /**
  * Destroy the chainstate manager options.
  */

</patch>
